articles.title: US activist returning from West Bank tour detained by Israeli police, UCPiP says
articles.summary:
US activist returning from West Bank tour detained by Israeli police, UCPiP says

Israeli police have detained Mel Duncan, co-founder of Unarmed Civilian Protection in Palestine (UCPiP), as he was returning to Tel Aviv after a tour of the occupied West Bank, the organisation said in a statement on X.

A US citizen from St. Paul, Minnesota, and a longtime advocate for nonviolence and civilian protection, Mel was not engaged in any illegal activity, UCPiP said.

"He was travelling on a bus full of Israeli citizens returning from a tour of the West Bank and heading towards Tel Aviv when Israeli police stopped the bus, held it for approximately an hour, and confiscated his passport. Mel was the only passenger detained," the statement read.

He is currently being held at Ma’ale Adumim police station, and the grounds for his detention remain unclear, the statement added.

His lawyer has requested urgent diplomatic intervention to ensure he is questioned tonight rather than spending two nights in detention. The organisation also urged the US Embassy in Israel, elected representatives and the international community to intervene and secure Mel's release.

🚨 URGENT ACTION ALERT: UCPiP Co-Founder Mel Duncan Detained by Israeli Police 27 November 2026 Mel Duncan, co-founder of Unarmed Civilian Protection in Palestine (UCPiP), a U.S. citizen from St. Paul, Minnesota, and a longtime advocate for nonviolence and civilian protection, was detained today by Israeli police. Mel was not engaged in any illegal activity. He was travelling on a bus full of Israeli citizens returning from a tour of the West Bank and heading towards Tel Aviv when Israeli police stopped the bus, held it for approximately an hour, and confiscated his passport. Mel was the only passenger detained. He is currently being held at Ma’ale Adumim police station. The grounds for his detention remain unclear. His lawyer has requested urgent diplomatic intervention to ensure he is questioned tonight rather than spending two nights in detention. We urgently call upon the U.S. Embassy, elected representatives and the international community to: ▪️ Intervene immediately to secure Mel’s release. ▪️ Ensure questioning takes place tonight without unnecessary delays. ▪️ Guarantee his safety, legal rights and access to consular assistance. Those who dedicate their lives to protecting civilians should not themselves become targets. Please circulate widely and contact the U.S. Embassy and your elected representatives immediately. Unarmed Civilian Protection in Palestine (UCPiP) https://t.co/kvfWQawXHk #FreeMelDuncan #ProtectTheProtectors #UCPiP

— UCP in Palestine (@ucpinpalestine) November 27, 2026

articles.title: Centcom rejects Iran's claims on warship attack, Hormuz shipping charges
articles.summary:
Centcom rejects Iran's claims on warship attack, Hormuz shipping charges

The United States Central Command (Centcom) has refuted the Iranian military's claim that Iran attacked the USS Abraham Lincoln on the first day of the war, or that the IRGC regained control of two Iranian oil tankers seized by the US forces.

In a post on X, Centcom also refuted Iran's charge that it was charging $2.5 million from ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

An Iranian military commander made multiple FALSE claims concerning U.S. Forces over the past 24 hours: 🚫 CLAIM: The U.S. military stole two Iranian oil tankers and the IRGC’s navy retook the vessels while American troops on board slept. ✅ FACT: Iran no longer has a navy. The entire situation the Iranian military commander described is another fabricated lie. 🚫 CLAIM: Iranian naval forces struck aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72) on the first day of Operation Epic Fury, forcing U.S. forces to seek assistance from regional countries for evacuation support. ✅ FACT: The Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group was well defended and never struck by Iran as a result. In fact, the strike group completed a historically successful combat deployment to the Middle East and safely returned to the United States last month. 🚫 CLAIM: CENTCOM is charging $2.5 million to ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. ✅ FACT: While U.S. forces and regional partners do control the Strait of Hormuz, there is no toll for passing ships. CENTCOM’s efforts have restored freedom of navigation through the international waterway. Thousands of ships and billions of crude oil barrels have transited the strait freely and safely under U.S. protection despite unwarranted Iranian aggression.

— U.S. Central Command (@CENTCOM) November 28, 2026

articles.title: Israeli defence minister rejects army chief's call to detain violent settlers, report says
articles.summary:
Israeli defence minister rejects army chief's call to detain violent settlers, report says

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has rejected a new request from military chief of staff Eyal Zamir to authorise administrative detention orders against Israeli settlers involved in attacks against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, Kan reported.

Zamir told Katz at a security consultation on Thursday that further steps were needed amid rising settler violence, and called for administrative detention and restraining orders against perpetrators, the report said.

Administrative detention allows suspects to be held indefinitely without charge or trial. It is widely used against Palestinians, including children, but Katz halted its use against Jewish Israelis in November 2024. He has, in fact,  repeatedly boasted of doing so, while expanding its use against Palestinians.

Dozens of restraining orders, which bar individuals from parts of the West Bank, are awaiting Shin Bet approval, according to Kan. Channel 12 reported that 70 people suspected of involvement in such attacks were arrested in recent weeks, but Israeli courts released all of them without indictments.

Shin Bet chief David Zini, who belongs to the Orthodox nationalist Hardal camp, has consistently objected to movement bans. He has been accused of undermining the agency's unit tasked with tackling settler violence.

articles.title: Israeli military claims MSF workers killed in Gaza strike were Hamas members
articles.summary:
Israeli military claims MSF workers killed in Gaza strike were Hamas members

The Israeli military has said the two Doctors Without Borders (MSF) workers -- Ahmed Sufyan Muhammad Ali Abu Hasira and Ma’ad Yousef Ali Sabeh -- killed in an air strike on a clinic in Gaza City were members of Hamas.

In a statement, the military said Ali Sabeh was as an artillery unit commander in Hamas’s armed wing, without providing any evidence. It denied targeting a hospital or damaging medical infrastructure, saying precautions had been taken to minimise civilian casualties.

articles.title: Oil, gas prices fall as Brent trims weekly gains ahead of OPEC+ meeting
articles.summary: Brent crude and European natural gas prices fell on Friday after a volatile week as traders weighed threats to Middle Eastern energy supplies against recovering Gulf oil shipments, Anadolu reports. Brent crude declined 2.3% to $94.15 a barrel as of 1715GMT, trimming its weekly gain to less than 2%. The international benchmark remained on track for its first weekly advance in November, while US benchmark West Texas Intermediate traded below $83 a barrel. European natural gas prices dropped 3.3% to €84.69 ($92.6) per megawatt-hour, bringing their weekly decline to more than 3%. Traders were assessing a possible recovery in Norwegian gas supplies following outages and maintenance, while colder weather threatened to increase heating demand. articles.summary: Four Palestinians were killed and several others, including women and children, were injured on Friday in Israeli attacks across Gaza despite a ceasefire agreement in effect since October 2025, Anadolu reports.
